findings.title: XCom serialization
findings.body:
The docs and docstring say the returned dict is safe to push to XCom. That only holds for primitive fields, because `output_parsed.model_dump()` uses the default Python mode. If a user's model has fields like `Enum`, `UUID`, `bytes`, or other custom or nested types, the dict keeps those Python objects. That can fail or round-trip unexpectedly when Airflow serializes the return value to XCom.

Use `model_dump(mode="json")` so the value is always JSON-compatible. This may not affect every field type, depending on Airflow's serde support, but `mode="json"` matches the documented guarantee.

findings.title: Inconsistent status handling
findings.body:
The structured path only fails when `output_parsed` is `None`. Unlike the existing `create_response` path, it never logs a warning when `parsed.status != "completed"`, so incomplete responses that still parse are returned silently.

The comment also says truncated responses lead to `None`. In the SDK, truncated or invalid JSON usually raises a pydantic `ValidationError` inside `responses.parse` instead, so the explanatory error message is never reached for that case.
